# Turn-by-turn navigation haptics and sound (2026-02-05 15:50Z)

_**User**_

I would like to introduce haptics and sound effect during turn-by-turn navigation (enabled by double-tapping when the navigation route is reversed).

When it's time to navigate for the current navigation instruction there should be haptic and sound feedback that allows the user to differentiate between left, right and straight routing instructions.

Sound should respect the system settings (quiet mode etc.) as with the sound effect for mutual navigation.

I will provide 3 sound effects and wiring should be alike the current mutual-navigation-sound effect

Control tracking, data retention, server URL, device autolock, accuracy indicators, map type, zoom level, update interval, group zoom‑to‑fit, off‑screen arrows, auto‑refresh, reverse geocoding threshold, navigation mode, and route progress.\\\\\\\\n- View location tracking details or replay the onboarding wizard.\\\\\\\\n- Settings are grouped into tracking, app behavior, map configuration, and navigation sections for easier discovery.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- All app preferences are also available in the system Settings app.\\\\\\\\n- New options include: navigation route auto‑update, route progress visualization toggle, a global pulsing/shimmer switch for map markers, and off‑screen arrow visibility.\\\\\\\\n- Bicycle transport mode was removed; existing values fall back to walking for directions and car icons where applicable.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;SettingsManager&#96; stores all preferences in &#96;UserDefaults&#96; and triggers side effects such as permission checks and auto‑refresh.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96; binds directly to these properties and navigates to &#96;iPhone_LocationStatusView&#96; (now a page) or re-runs the onboarding flow via &#96;AppState&#96;.\\\\\\\\n- Defaults are registered from &#96;Settings.bundle&#96;, enabling control from the system Settings app. The manager observes low‑power state and scene phase for UI effect gating.\\\\\\\\n- Reverse geocoding threshold is user‑configurable (off/100 m/1 km/10 km; default 1 km) and applied centrally.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Location Status &amp; Error Handling\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\n- A dedicated status view shows permission state, last GPS and server updates, background activity, and a log of recent events.\\\\\\\\n- If a network or permission error occurs, an overlay explains the problem.\\\\\\\\n- Map screens additionally display a network-error icon when the server cannot be reached.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- The status view lists speed and battery (when available) and tracks route‑request statistics over the last 24 hours.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; posts &#96;didSendOwnLocationUpdate&#96; notifications; &#96;ErrorOverlayManager&#96; and &#96;ErrorOverlay&#96; provide reusable alert UIs, and map views toggle a network icon via &#96;showNetworkErrorIcon&#96; flags.\\\\\\\\n- Status is presented as a dedicated page; related counters (e.g., daily route requests) are maintained in settings/state for Wire the overlay into the navigation view\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\\\\\\\\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.\\\\\\\\n- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:\\\\\\\\n  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)\\\\\\\\n  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)\\\\\\\\n  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\\\\\\\\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\\\\\\\\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\\\\\\\\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\\\\\\\\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"name: Navigation Overlay Mode\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"overview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"todos:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  - When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\\\\\\\\n- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.\\\\\\\\n- Route progress can be visualized using completed vs. remaining segments with a moving ghost marker (shown after at least 5% estimated progress).\\\\\\\\n- Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.\\\\\\\\n- Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.\\\\\\\\n- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&#96; draws markers, off‑screen arrows, error overlays, network‑error icons, and handles map camera logic, timers, and edit/navigation sheets. to show live turn‑by‑turn instructions when routing from the current device toward the target device.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96; estimates remote progress along the route using last update timestamps and current/estimated speed; Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\\\\\\\\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\\\\\\\\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\\\\\\\\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\\\\\\\\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"name: Navigation Overlay Mode\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"overview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"todos:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  - Navigation Overlay Mode\\\\\\\\noverview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\\\\\\\\ntodos:\\\\\\\\n  - id: overlay-wireup\\\\\\\\n    content: Wire overlay view/model into docs-changelog\\\\\\\\n    content: Update CHANGELOG and feature docs\\\\\\\\n    status: completed\\\\\\\\nisProject: false\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Implementation plan\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 1) Wire the overlay into the navigation view\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- In &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; add a &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel&#96; state object and create/update it when a route is calculated and the mode is “current device → other device” (&#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;).\\\\\\\\n- Place the overlay at the top of the map overlay stack in &#96;mapWithModifiers&#96; so it appears above the map but below other system overlays. This lines up with the existing overlay structure and your UI preference.\\\\\\\\n- Ensure the overlay is hidden when:\\\\\\\\n  - &#96;isRouteReversed == true&#96; (device → user mode)\\\\\\\\n  - &#96;route == nil&#96; (no route)\\\\\\\\n  - Navigation has been auto-stopped (route cleared)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2) Keep instructions in sync with live location\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- On each location update (&#96;locationManager.$currentLocation&#96;) update the overlay view model’s current step based on the user’s position on the route.\\\\\\\\n- When the route is recalculated (manual reload, auto-update, or transport type change), reset the overlay view model with the new &#96;MKRoute&#96; and restart at step 0.\\\\\\\\n- If the route is swapped via the toolbar button, recreate the overlay view model only when switching to &#96;isRouteReversed == false&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3) Handle edge cases and side effects\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Ensure that cached routes still populate the overlay view model when the cached route is applied, not only when a new network route is fetched.\\\\\\\\n- When &#96;stopNavigation()&#96; clears the route, also clear/hide the overlay to avoid stale instructions.\\\\\\\\n- Confirm the overlay responds correctly to &#96;mapUpdateInterval&#96; auto-updates and to mutual navigation changes (no changes required, but verify no overlay conflicts).\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"name: Navigation Overlay Mode\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"overview: Add NavigationOverlayKit to show turn-by-turn instructions when navigation is switched to “from current device → other device”, updating the overlay in sync with route recalculation and live location updates, and document the change.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"todos:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  - When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\\\\\\\\n- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.\\\\\\\\n- Route progress can be visualized using completed vs. remaining segments with a moving ghost marker (shown after at least 5% estimated progress).\\\\\\\\n- Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.\\\\\\\\n- Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.\\\\\\\\n- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&#96; draws markers, off‑screen arrows, error overlays, network‑error icons, and handles map camera logic, timers, and edit/navigation sheets. Auto‑centering gating is unified across views.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; uses &#96;MKRoute&#96;, &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96;, and &#96;SettingsManager.navigationTransportType&#96; to render routes and progress; it recalculates on transport changes or movement thresholds and enforces a daily route‑request limit.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;NavigationOverlayKit&#96; is used in &#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&#96; to show live turn‑by‑turn instructions when routing from the current device toward the target device.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96; estimates remote progress along the route using last update timestamps and current/estimated speed; progress overlay rendering splits polylines into completed/remaining segments.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; is backed by &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96; for cached updates; &#96;MapCompass&#96; is shared.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96; groups arrow indicators by edge and scales coordinates; segments represent ~50 km and are capped at 10.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and label components use rasterized caching keyed by color/icon/height/colorScheme/scale and respect Dynamic Type and color scheme.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":67},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass;                   "lineNumber": 1471,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\\n- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.\\n- Route progress can be visualized using completed vs. remaining segments with a moving ghost marker (shown after at least 5% estimated progress).\\n- Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.\\n- Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.\\n- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&amp;#9 [... omitted end of long line]"

                  "lineNumber": 14937,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- When enabled, other known devices that would be visible at the current zoom level are shown on a device’s map for better context.\\n- Navigation includes a scale bar and custom compass; auto‑centering pauses while you interact and resumes automatically once idle.\\n- Route progress can be visualized using completed vs. remaining segments with a moving ghost marker (shown after at least 5% estimated progress).\\n- Routes are recalculated when transport mode changes or after significant movement; route requests are rate‑limited daily, and the reload action can force a fresh calculation ignoring caches.\\n- Start navigation by long‑pressing a device pin on the map or swiping right on a device row. Your own device never offers navigation. Apple Maps handoff uses proper destination names.\\n- When you switch navigation to route from your device toward a selected device, a top overlay displays turn‑by‑turn instructions.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_DeviceMapView&amp;#9 [... omitted end of long line]"

                  "content": "- [ ] H4: Multiple simultaneous calls to refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() cause overlay to flip between states"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15294,
                  "content": "- [ ] H5: Location updates trigger updateNavigationOverlayStep() with old route while new route is being calculated"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15306,
                  "content": "Setting &#96;lastOverlayStepIndex = nil&#96; before setting step 0 causes &#96;updateNavigationOverlayStep()&#96; to immediately recalculate. Setting &#96;lastOverlayStepIndex = 0&#96; after initializing step 0 to prevent immediate recalculation:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15353,
                  "content": "Fixed: when refreshing the overlay, &#96;lastOverlayStepIndex&#96; was set to &#96;nil&#96; before setting step 0, so &#96;updateNavigationOverlayStep()&#96; immediately recalculated and could change the step, causing flickering."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15404,
                  "content": "- [x] H1: When isRouteReversed toggles, refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() is called with old route before new route calculation completes"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15405,
                  "content": "- [x] H2: updateNavigationOverlayStep() is called during async route calculation using stale route reference"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15407,
                  "content": "- [ ] H4: Multiple simultaneous calls to refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() cause overlay to flip between states"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15408,
                  "content": "- [ ] H5: Location updates trigger updateNavigationOverlayStep() with old route while new route is being calculated"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15492,
                  "content": "Added instrumentation to track route recalculation. When routes are recalculated during navigation (e.g., device moves off route), &#96;refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()&#96; resets to step 0, which can show \"Continue\"."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15538,
                  "content": "Logs show that when routes are recalculated, &#96;refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()&#96; resets to step 0, and &#96;updateNavigationOverlayStep()&#96; then calculates the remaining distance, which can be 0m if the user is already past step 0, causing \"Continue 0m\"."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15548,
                  "content": "- [x] H1: When isRouteReversed toggles, refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() is called with old route before new route calculation completes"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15549,
                  "content": "- [x] H2: updateNavigationOverlayStep() is called during async route calculation using stale route reference"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15551,
                  "content": "- [ ] H4: Multiple simultaneous calls to refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute() cause overlay to flip between states"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15552,
                  "content": "- [ ] H5: Location updates trigger updateNavigationOverlayStep() with old route while new route is being calculated"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15597,
                  "content": "Fixed: when refreshing the overlay, it always started at step 0. If the user was already past step 0, &#96;updateNavigationOverlayStep()&#96; calculated 0m remaining, causing \"Continue 0m\"."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15782,
                  "content": "Checking whether NavigationOverlayViewModel shows a default step on creation so one frame can show \"Arrive at destination\" before we call &#96;update(step:)&#96;."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15796,
                  "content": "  \"pattern\": \"NavigationOverlayViewModel|NavigationOverlayKit\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15807,
                  "content": "    \"pattern\": \"NavigationOverlayViewModel|NavigationOverlayKit\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15923,
                  "content": "**Cause:** The overlay was updated in two steps: first &#96;navigationOverlayViewModel = NavigationOverlayViewModel(...)&#96;, then &#96;update(step:)&#96; and &#96;updateRemainingDistance(...)&#96;. SwiftUI could render in between, so for one frame the view used the kit’s default step (often the last step, “Arrive at destination”) before your step was applied."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15927,
                  "content": "1. Create &#96;newViewModel = NavigationOverlayViewModel(route: route, unit: ...)&#96;."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15990,
                  "content": "Adding the same safeguard in &#96;updateNavigationOverlayStep()&#96; so we don't switch to \"Arrive at destination\" during navigation when the user is still far."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 16051,
                  "content": "1. **&#96;refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()&#96;**  "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 16054,
                  "content": "2. **&#96;updateNavigationOverlayStep()&#96;**  "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 16649,
                  "content": "3. **“Arrive at destination” safeguard:** In both &#96;refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()&#96; and &#96;updateNavigationOverlayStep()&#96;, if the chosen step is the last one, check the distance from the user to the destination. If it’s more than 150 m, use step 0 instead so “Arrive at destination” only appears when the user is actually near the destination."
                },

                  "content": "   In &#96;onChange(of: isRouteReversed)&#96;, we now clear &#96;route&#96;, &#96;travelTime&#96;, &#96;distanceText&#96;, and the overlay (&#96;navigationOverlayViewModel&#96;, &#96;lastOverlayStepIndex&#96;) instead of calling &#96;refreshNavigationOverlayForCurrentRoute()&#96;. That avoids showing the old route/overlay while the new one is calculated."

The view never sees the kit’s default “Arrive at destination” frame."

If it’s more than 150 m, we use step 0 so “Arrive at destination” only appears when the user is actually near the destination."

@StateObject private var viewModel = NavigationOverlayViewModel()
@State private var cancellables = Set<AnyCancellable>()
this is the example code to tap into the NavigationOverlayKit symbol 
func bindHaptics() {
    viewModel.$symbol
        .compactMap { $0 }
        .sink { symbol in
            let generator: UIImpactFeedbackGenerator
            switch symbol {
            case .uTurn, .arrive:
                generator = UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .heavy)
            case .left, .right, .sharpLeft, .sharpRight:
                generator = UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .medium)
            case .slightLeft, .slightRight:
                generator = UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .light)
            case .start, .straight, .cross, .tunnel, .bridge, .stairs, .escalator:
                generator = UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .soft)
            }
            generator.impactOccurred()
        }
        .store(in: &cancellables)
}
